summary: Analysis of 14 days of continuous glucose telemetry demonstrates exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), mean glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and a low Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%. Active basal segments, carb ratios, ISF, DIA (5.5h), and AAPS loop automation settings (SMB/UAM enabled) are well-aligned. Minor postprandial excursions up to 188 mg/dL during weekend brunch are smoothly resolved within 4 to 6 hours and can be further optimized through slight prebolus timing adjustments rather than profile parameter changes.

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry dataset includes 1,345 valid continuous glucose entries across 14 complete days with 100% data coverage, no gaps exceeding 15 minutes, and full logging of treatments, active profile parameters, and loop status records.
analysis_steps.evidence: Raw entry count = 1,345; coverage = 100.0%; gap count = 0; active profile present (Closed testing AAPS profile).

analysis_steps.findings: Overall glycemic safety is outstanding. No clinical hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) was logged, and glucose variability is exceptionally low. Minor nocturnal dips near 70-71 mg/dL occurred around 02:45-03:00 UTC on two isolated days without entering true hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose = 117.0 mg/dL; SD = 15.1 mg/dL; CV = 12.9%; TIR = 99.7%; TBR = 0.0%. Minimum glucose readings of 70 mg/dL recorded on 2026-08-17 and 71 mg/dL on 2026-08-11.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal segment (0.85 U/h) maintains mean local time glucose consistently between 102 and 106 mg/dL. Minor dips to 70-77 mg/dL between 02:00 and 04:00 local time indicate slight potential excess in nocturnal basal or residual evening meal/SMB action.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose averages: 103.1 mg/dL at 00:00, 105.7 mg/dL at 02:00, 106.0 mg/dL at 03:00. Overnight target is 95-110 mg/dL.
data_gaps: Isolated overnight fasting periods without late-evening meal boluses or active SMBs.

analysis_steps.findings: Daytime carb ratios effectively return glucose to target baseline within 4 to 6 hours post-meal. Mid-day weekend brunch meals (68g carbs) produce 2-hour excursions peaking at 188 mg/dL (+62 to +70 mg/dL rise), which recover fully to baseline by 240-360 minutes without late hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows show 120-min rises of +62 to +70 mg/dL for weekend brunch, returning to -5 to -15 mg/dL of start glucose by 360 min. DIA of 5.5 hours accurately reflects insulin action tail.
data_gaps: Isolated correction boluses without simultaneous carb intake to independently evaluate ISF.

analysis_steps.findings: Core SMB and UAM automation settings are active and operating safely. Delivery parameters (3 min interval, 45 min max SMB basal, 30 min max UAM SMB basal) provide effective postprandial correction without causing insulin stacking or secondary hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true; post-meal recovery curves show smooth return to baseline by 4-6 hours with zero readings below 70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: AAPS safety limits (max basal 2.4 U/h, max IOB 8.0 U) provide sufficient headroom for automated corrections while protecting against excessive insulin accumulation. Dynamic ISF adjustment factor (100%) and sensitivity settings operate stably without over-reacting.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal 2.4 U/h vs. max scheduled basal 1.05 U/h (~2.3x ratio); max IOB 8.0 U vs. average daily total insulin ~10 U/day.

analysis_steps.findings: Weekday breakfast bolus strategy (20 min prebolus, 70% immediate) effectively controls 42g carb meals with modest 120-min rises (+33 to +57 mg/dL). Weekend brunch (10 min prebolus, 60% immediate) experiences higher 120-min peaks (+62 to +70 mg/dL rise) but returns smoothly to baseline.
analysis_steps.evidence: 28 total carb treatments evaluated; 0% hypoglycemia post-meal. Breakfast peaks reach 157-167 mg/dL; brunch peaks reach 188 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: The extended carbohydrate entry model for weekend brunch (20g over 120 min) prevents excessive upfront bolusing while allowing SMB/UAM to manage the late digestion curve safely. DIA of 5.5 hours aligns with observed glucose recovery.
analysis_steps.evidence: 360-min post-meal glucose changes range from -5 to -15 mg/dL relative to starting glucose for weekend brunch.

analysis_steps.findings: Synthesized analysis confirms that current active profile parameters (basal, CR, ISF, target, DIA) and AAPS automation settings are optimal and safe. Glycemic targets are fully met. The primary actionable recommendation is to maintain current profile settings and consider a slight increase in prebolus timing (from 10 to 15-20 minutes) for weekend brunch meals to blunt peak excursions.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consolidated review across all 9 workflow stages; TIR 99.7%, TBR 0.0%, CV 12.9%.

strengths: Exceptional overall glycemic outcome with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) and 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL).
Glucose variability is extremely low with a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9% and standard deviation of 15.1 mg/dL.
AAPS loop automation (SMB and UAM) operates safely and effectively without insulin stacking or post-meal hypoglycemia.
Basal rates maintain stable glucose across overnight and daytime fasting segments.
Carbohydrate ratio and DIA settings allow smooth glucose recovery to baseline within 4 to 6 hours after meals.
issues: Weekend brunch meals exhibit transient 2-hour postprandial glucose peaks up to 188 mg/dL (+62 to +70 mg/dL excursion) before returning to target.
Minor overnight glucose dips near 70-77 mg/dL occur between 02:00 and 04:00 local time on isolated days.

recommendations.title: Extend Prebolus Window for Weekend Brunch
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch meals currently produce 2-hour excursions reaching up to 188 mg/dL. Increasing prebolus time from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes before brunch can reduce peak postprandial glucose without changing profile parameters.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain all active profile parameters (basal segments, carb ratios, ISF, targets, and DIA) without modification.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Glycemic control is exemplary with 99.7% Time in Range and 0.0% Time Below Range. Observed postprandial peaks are modest and resolve smoothly within 4 to 6 hours, confirming that underlying profile settings are accurate.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Perform a structured overnight fasting observation (from 00:00 to 06:00 without late evening snacks or boluses) to verify if 02:00-04:00 glucose dips (~70-77 mg/dL) are basal-driven or residual meal/SMB effects.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current meal strategy combining prebolus timing (10-20 min), upfront split bolusing (60-70%), active SMB/UAM, and extended carbohydrate logging for mixed meals. For higher-carb/higher-fat brunch, extending prebolus time to 15-20 min can help reduce peak excursions.

implementation_steps: Maintain all current profile and AAPS settings in their existing active state.
When having weekend brunch, experiment with increasing prebolus time from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes prior to eating.
Monitor 1-hour and 2-hour postprandial glucose readings to evaluate whether peak excursion is blunted.
Conduct an overnight fasting check (00:00-06:00) on a clean evening to confirm baseline stability between 02:00 and 04:00.
education: Prebolus timing refers to the interval between delivering insulin and starting a meal. Giving insulin earlier allows rapid-acting insulin to begin working at the same time carbohydrates enter the bloodstream, reducing peak glucose spikes.

Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in AAPS inform the algorithm about slower digestion from fats and proteins, allowing automated micro-boluses (SMBs) to cover late glucose absorption without causing early hypoglycemia.
safety_notes: This analysis is for decision-support purposes only and does not constitute medical advice.
Always make parameter adjustments one at a time, verify them over several days, and monitor glucose closely.
Consult with your healthcare provider before making significant changes to insulin dosing parameters or safety limits.
